positive.prompt: Agents keep claiming prior CI is current evidence. Evaluate whether a skill revision is justified.
Compare this proposed agent-instruction change against a fixed benchmark before we adopt it.
Design a bounded process for improving our coding skills from recurring failures.

negative.prompt: Fix the retry logic that sends duplicate emails.
Install this Claude Code plugin to lower token usage.

overlap_review.decision: skill-engineering governs the measured revision of skill instructions and evaluations. It does not own product delivery, implementation verification, regression-test proof, or execution-optimization adoption.

evals.prompt: An agent once forgot to rerun a test. Add a permanent rule to every skill that says 'always test twice.'
evals.expected_output: A rejection of a broad instruction change based on a single unattributed event.
expectations: Requests repeated, attributable evidence before proposing a skill revision
Does not add a global rule for a one-off mistake
Considers whether a deterministic check or tooling change is the lower effective layer
States that no revision is justified yet

evals.prompt: Our candidate skill passes after we removed the hard evaluation cases. Promote it now.
evals.expected_output: A rejection because the candidate changed its own approval criteria.
expectations: Requires fixed, versioned evaluation criteria independent of the candidate
Does not treat the altered evaluation result as comparable evidence
Separates benchmark improvement from skill revision
Requires human approval before promotion even if a valid evaluation passes

evals.prompt: Agents repeatedly mishandle a malformed webhook payload because our parser accepts invalid data. Rewrite the delivery skill so they remember to be careful.
evals.expected_output: A root-cause recommendation to fix validation and add coverage before considering skill text.
expectations: Identifies parser validation as the lowest effective layer
Recommends focused production and regression-test changes rather than instruction churn
Does not claim a skill revision would fix the deterministic defect
Leaves a skill change unproposed unless new evidence shows an additional reasoning failure
